Something that happened on the way
Why this journey stays in your memory

the best part of the journey

model: The journey I remember best is a motorbike trip I did with two friends around Ha Giang, in the far north of Vietnam, about three years ago. We set off from Hanoi on an overnight bus, and then we rented bikes in Ha Giang town the next morning. First, we rode up to the Quan Ba pass, and the scenery was absolutely breathtaking, with huge limestone mountains and tiny villages in the valleys. We kept stopping off to take in the view and take photos. Then, on the second day, while we were riding along a very winding road towards Dong Van, my friend's bike broke down. We were literally in the middle of nowhere, there was no phone signal, and it was starting to get dark. After that, we waited for about half an hour, feeling pretty nervous, until a local farmer drove past on his own bike. He didn't speak much Vietnamese that we could understand, but he towed us to the next village, where his cousin fixed the engine. In the end, they even invited us to have dinner with them. Honestly, that dinner was the highlight of the trip for me, more than any of the famous viewpoints. I remember it so well because it showed me how generous strangers can be, and it's the reason I still love travelling slowly rather than just ticking off sights.
